description: Canonical vocabulary of PATIENT attributes that feed protocol-fit / friction analysis. Parallel axis to burden_categories.json (which names the burden) and content_sources.json (which names the voice's origin). This registry names WHO the patient is. Each attribute is read by friction rules (persona_predicate.attr) and is the shape a research-derived indication baseline will populate. NOTE: this is a v0 SYNTHETIC draft — value bands and the drives[] mapping are placeholders for shaping the model, not research-backed numbers. US-first; geography/country modifiers are deferred (see WORKBENCH_PLAN site-readiness axis). The `axis` field separates CAPACITY (what the patient can physically do) from WILLINGNESS (what they'll choose to do) from CLINICAL/DEMOGRAPHIC — the LN-vs-MS contrast needs capacity AND willingness to diverge independently. The `grain` field marks whether an attribute is meaningful as an indication-level population prior (`indication_baseline`) or only per-person (`individual`). The `status` field marks whether the attribute already exists in code (`exists`) or is proposed (`new`).

axes.label: Capacity — what the patient can physically pull off
Willingness — what the patient will choose to do

items.label: Physical / functional capacity
items.description: What the body can tolerate across a long visit day, multi-day windows, and travel. Anchorable to a disease PRO (e.g. EDSS for MS). Core of the LN-vs-MS contrast — MS skews lower.

items.label: Fatigue burden
items.description: Cumulative fatigue load — compounds across back-to-back timepoints (e.g. D4/D7/D10) and travel days.

items.label: Mobility-aid dependence
items.description: Reliance on mobility aids — bears on site accessibility, inpatient stays, and imaging logistics.

items.label: Comorbidity load
items.description: Concurrent-condition burden — affects eligibility, procedure risk, and monitoring intensity.

items.label: Distance to Center of Excellence
items.description: Travel distance to the trial site. Already read by distant_routine_followup and specialist_imaging_far. Population prior is weak; better as individual or geography-derived.

items.label: Caregiver availability
items.description: Availability of a support partner for discharge, post-infusion no-driving windows, and inpatient stays. Read by inpatient_caregiver_required and caregiver_required_procedure.

items.label: Work flexibility
items.description: Ability to shift visits onto non-working days. Read by tight_window_consecutive, fasting_lab_morning_slot, twenty_four_hour_urine_at_home.

items.label: Urban / rural
items.description: Population density of the patient's location — proxy for site density and travel time.

items.label: Dependent-care load
items.description: Competing caregiving the patient is responsible for — bears on multi-day and inpatient feasibility.

items.label: Socioeconomic band
items.description: Socioeconomic band (from corpora speaker_attrs.ses). Underpins financial-burden friction.

items.label: Income-loss tolerance
items.description: How much unpaid time off the patient can absorb — bears on long follow-up tails and inpatient stays.

items.label: Insurance type (US)
items.description: US coverage type — bears on standard-of-care coverage during the trial and access. US-specific.

items.label: Out-of-pocket sensitivity
items.description: Sensitivity to travel/lodging/incidental costs — drives the need for stipends.

items.label: Disease pattern
items.description: Course shape over time (MS relapsing→progressive; LN flare/remission). Bears on windowing tolerance, urgency, and dropout risk.

items.label: Condition stage
items.description: Disease stage (per-indication semantics; from corpora condition_stage_at_speech). Bears on eligibility and monitoring intensity.

items.label: Progression rate
items.description: Rate of deterioration — fast progression raises pre-treatment-ineligibility risk in a long CAR-T pathway (per the ABZT-411 review's exclusion of rapidly-worsening renal function).

items.label: Renal stability
items.description: Indication-specific (LN). The ABZT-411 review recommends excluding rapidly-declining patients — this acts as an eligibility gate, not just a burden modifier.

items.label: Prior treatment failures
items.description: Count of prior failed therapies. Read by renal_biopsy_invasiveness; also a proxy for trial motivation in refractory populations.

items.label: Immunosuppression level
items.description: Background immunosuppression — bears on infection risk and vaccination gating before CAR-T (per the review's safety subgroups).

items.label: Travel tolerance
items.description: WILLINGNESS to travel, distinct from distance_to_coe_band (CAPACITY). The LN-vs-MS spine: an LN patient may travel nationally for a curative shot while an MS patient with the same distance will not.

items.label: Risk tolerance
items.description: Appetite for invasive procedures and novel-MoA therapy — bears on biopsy/leukapheresis acceptance.

items.label: Trial motivation
items.description: Why the patient is in the trial — predicts dropout risk across long protocols.

items.label: Procedure aversion
items.description: Aversion to invasive/repeated procedures (biopsy, LP, repeated bloods, leukapheresis).

items.label: Psychological burden
items.description: Self-reported psychological burden. Read by ice_repeated_cognitive_burden.

items.label: Health literacy
items.description: Ability to navigate consent complexity and self-managed assessments.

items.label: Decision-complexity tolerance
items.description: Tolerance for the informed-consent burden of a gene-modified-therapy + 15-year-LTFU decision.

items.label: Age band
items.description: Individual-only. A distribution at the indication level, not a single value — do not average into a baseline.

items.label: Sex assigned at birth
items.description: Individual-only. Carried per-person; an indication-level distribution at most.

items.label: Childbearing potential
items.description: Individual-only. Read by pregnancy_test_follow_up_cadence — drives extended contraception + repeat-testing burden.
